_note: ENTRY SURFACES vs DISPATCHER ROLE. An ENTRY SURFACE is where a person TYPES a request (any host they like). The DISPATCHER ROLE (classify, stamp review depth, brief, assign seats, run the risk gate, refill, and fan work OUT to the orchestration tree — sub-agents + specialist seats) is held by exactly ONE provider at a time, recorded in `dispatcher.provider`. DISPATCH IS USER-ASSIGNED, NEVER AN ABSOLUTE VALUE: any dispatch-capable provider the user owns may hold it. Rankings never grant this authority. In THIS owner's setup that assignment is the Claude orchestration surface (opus-5); a user with no Claude seat may assign a Codex/GPT surface (see config/examples/two-sub) — both are legitimate. The assigned dispatcher preserves its own account quota by DISPATCHING, not implementing (read-only legwork via a sub-agent is fine); it delegates. A non-dispatcher surface classifies + drafts a brief and hands it to the assigned dispatcher; it never self-assigns other seats or implements outside its own seat. To move the dispatcher, edit `dispatcher.provider` and the `can_dispatch` flags here; policy prose does not change.

dispatcher.rule: Exactly one dispatcher holds the classify/brief/assign/risk-gate and fans work out to the orchestration tree (sub-agents + seats). In this setup the assigned dispatcher is the Claude orchestration surface; it preserves its account by dispatching, not implementing. If the assigned dispatcher's whole pipe is down (here the Anthropic pipe via teamclaude — which also takes the Opus review pass, so it is ONE outage), the owner at the console may hand a COMPLETE brief straight to the implementer for non-gate work; gate work parks. A phone surface never implements.

claude-code.note: The surface the user assigned as dispatcher here (dispatcher.provider = opus-5) — the Claude orchestration surface. Full dispatch: classify, stamp review depth, brief, assign, gate, refill, and fan work OUT to the orchestration tree of sub-agents (other Claude profiles/seats) + the specialist seats. Preserves its own account quota by dispatching, not implementing (read-only legwork via a sub-agent is fine). This machine's /orchestrate runs in this mode.

codex-cli.note: In this setup a worker/review seat: GPT Terra runs Google-MCP volume and Codex Sol is the OpenAI review family (cross-family gate #2). Not the assigned dispatcher here, so if typed into it classifies + drafts a brief and hands it to the assigned dispatcher. Codex is dispatch-capable — a user who owns no Claude seat may legitimately assign it as their dispatcher (see config/examples/two-sub).

cursor.note: IDE surface, non-dispatcher here: classify + draft a brief, then hand it to the assigned dispatcher. Do not re-home dispatch onto the IDE unless the user assigns it here.

phone.note: Read status, forward briefs/reports to the assigned dispatcher, approve owner gates. Never implements or dispatches.

rules.non_dispatcher_hosts: classify + stamp + draft brief, then hand it to the assigned dispatcher (dispatcher.provider); never self-assign other seats or implement outside the surface's own seat
rules.entry_is_free: Any surface may be where a request starts. Where a request is TYPED is the user's choice; who DISPATCHES is a single user-assigned provider (dispatcher.provider), not a fixed identity.
rules.portability: Dispatch is user-assigned. Point `dispatcher.provider` at any dispatch-capable provider you own and mark that surface `can_dispatch:true` (this setup: the Claude orchestration surface; two-sub: a Codex/GPT surface; solo-pro: the single Claude seat). Exactly one holds it at a time; only the holder moves. See subscriptions.json portability_examples and USER-GUIDE.md §Entry points.
